messages.subject: Formative Higher-Order Models: Reflective first-order, formative second-order
parts:
Dear Lavaan users, 
I am trying to estimate a formative higher-order CFA model: Reflective first-order measurement model, formative second-order structure. This model is specified by Jarvis et al (p. 205): A Critical Review of Construct Indicators and Measurement Model Misspecification in Marketing and Consumer Research, Cheryl Burke Jarvis,  Scott B. MacKenzie,  and Philip M. Podsakoff, Journal of Consumer Research ,  Vol. 30,  No. 2 (September 2003),  pp. 199-218

I test the following model in Lavaan:

#   CFA TRUST TiP MZ1.
TIP_model <-   '
BW =~ X1 + X2 + X3
MI =~ X4 + X5 + X6
FK =~ X7 + X8 + X9
TiP <~ MI + BW + FK '

fit <-sem(TIP_model, data = TRUST_Study, estimator="ML")
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, modindices = TRUE)

The model is identified, yet I get the following error messages:

In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options = lavaanOptions,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

Error in solve.default(Q22) : 
  Lapackroutine dgesv: System ist exactly singular: U[19,19] = 0


Anyone an idea how I need to specify the model in Lavaan or why I get the error messages?

Thanks. Tobias

I disagree -- this model is not identified because the TiP construct is undefined.  I'm unfamiliar with the particular article you cited, but if you review either of the attached articles that discuss formative "measurement," you'll see that a formative construct is only "identified" if it is predicting at least one endogenous observed variable or latent construct that is locally identified in its own right.

I use the quotation marks because I have a hard time considering this to be a measurement model at all.  I can't argue with psychometricians like MacCallum and Bollen, who are infinitely smarter than I am and have written on the topic of formative measurement, but I can't shake the impression that the prospect of formative measurement is illusory.  If you are familiar with phantom constructs, you might notice that the only situations in which a formative construct is identified is when it can be interpreted as a phantom construct for whatever dependent variable(s) it predicts.  If there are multiple DVs it predicts, you can also interpret it as a latent construct (reflectively) defined by those DVs, which is being predicted by the IVs you think of as formative indicators.

It wouldn't be appropriate to start a discussion about formative measurement on this blog, but similar to the need to consider alternative equivalent models, I wanted to point out alternative interpretations of the same model you are trying to fit (if you find a way to identify the TiP construct).

Terry
